title: Chapter 1: Network Fundamentals — review questions
summary: 9 multiple-choice questions from chapter 1, with answers. 13 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: A switch receives a frame whose destination MAC address is not in its MAC address table. What does it do?
options: Sends it back out of the port it arrived on
Floods it out of all other ports
questions.why: unknown unicast frames are flooded out of every port except the incoming one.

questions.q: Which feature lets an NGFW allow a company app but block a game running on the same port?
questions.why: AVC identifies the application, not only the port number.

questions.q: Which layer of the 3-tier model should avoid access lists and packet filtering, and why?
questions.why: the core should switch traffic as fast as possible; policy belongs in the distribution layer.

questions.q: In a spine-leaf design, what do spine switches connect to?
questions.why: spines connect only to leaves; every leaf connects to every spine.

questions.q: You must run 10 Gbps over copper for 90 metres in a new building. Which cable do you choose?
questions.why: Cat6a supports 10GBASE-T to 100 m. Cat6 only reaches about 55 m, and Cat5e is not supported.

questions.q: Which pins are crossed to make a 10/100 crossover cable?
questions.why: pin 1 goes to pin 3 and pin 2 goes to pin 6. For gigabit you also cross 47 and 58.

questions.q: A company has a small campus and wants to save money while keeping most hierarchy benefits. Which design fits?
questions.why: a collapsed core merges the core and distribution layers into one set of switches.

questions.q: Which statement about a Layer 2 switch is TRUE?
options: It creates one collision domain for all ports
It creates one broadcast domain per port
It builds its table from source MAC addresses
It forwards frames based on IP addresses
questions.why: a switch learns from source MAC addresses. It makes one collision domain per port and does not split broadcast domains.

questions.q: Which standard delivers up to 15.4 W at the port?
questions.why: 802.3af (PoE) gives 15.4 W at the PSE.

title: Chapter 2: TCP/IP — review questions
summary: 9 multiple-choice questions from chapter 2, with answers. 22 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: Which protocol sends passwords in clear text and should not be used on production networks?
questions.why: Telnet has no encryption. SSH replaces it.

questions.q: Which two features does TCP have that UDP does not?
questions.why: TCP adds sequencing, acknowledgments, windowing and connections. Both protocols use ports and checksums.

questions.q: Host A at 192.168.1.10/24 pings Host B on another subnet. What destination MAC address does Host A put on the first frame?
questions.why: for a remote destination the frame goes to the gateway. The IP packet inside still has Host B's address.

questions.q: What class is 191.255.1.1? What is its default mask?
questions.why: 128-191 is Class B.

questions.q: Which address is a Layer 2 broadcast?
questions.why: 255.255.255.255 is a Layer 3 broadcast; 224.0.0.10 is multicast; 127.0.0.1 is loopback.

questions.q: What must happen after a DHCP IP conflict is detected?
options: The client uses a gratuitous ARP to fix it
An administrator must resolve it by hand before the address is reused
The server gives both hosts new addresses
questions.why: the conflicting address is removed from the pool until an administrator fixes the conflict.

questions.q: Which protocol sets up a secure session similar to Telnet?
questions.why: SSH encrypts the session.

questions.q: Which mechanism does a DHCP client use to check for a duplicate address?
questions.why: the client broadcasts an ARP for its own new address.

questions.q: Which two statements describe a DHCP Discover? (Choose two.)
questions.why: and B - it is a broadcast at Layers 2 and 3 and uses UDP.

title: Chapter 3: Easy Subnetting — review questions
summary: 9 multiple-choice questions from chapter 3, with answers. 13 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: How many subnets does a /26 give you from a Class C network (subnet-zero allowed)?
questions.why: 2 borrowed bits give 2� = 4 subnets: 0, 64, 128, 192.

questions.q: What are the subnet and broadcast addresses of 192.168.20.133/27?
questions.why: block size 32: 128, 160  133 is in the 128 subnet; broadcast = 160 - 1 = 159; hosts .129 - .158.

questions.q: What are the subnet and broadcast addresses of 172.20.45.130/20?
questions.why: /20  block 16 in the third octet: 32, 48  45 is in 32; broadcast = 48.0 - 1 = 47.255.

questions.q: How many subnets and hosts per subnet does 172.16.0.0/19 give?
questions.why: 3 bits borrowed = 8 subnets (subnet-zero allowed); 13 host bits = 8,190 hosts. If subnet-zero were disallowed you would count 6 or 7.

questions.q: How many usable host addresses does the 255.255.255.224 mask give per subnet?
questions.why: 224 means 5 host bits: 25 - 2 = 30.

questions.q: You need 29 subnets and as many hosts per subnet as possible from a Class C network. How many bits do you borrow?
questions.why: 24 = 16 is too few; 25 = 32 � 29, so borrow 5 bits (/29), giving 6 hosts per subnet.

questions.q: What subnet does 200.10.5.68/28 belong to?
Which statement about subnet-zero is correct?
options: It is off by default in modern IOS
It lets you use the first subnet
It adds two hosts per subnet
questions.why: it allows the all-zeros subnet; it is on by default.

questions.q: Which three subnets are valid for a /27 on 192.168.4.0?
questions.why: valid subnets are multiples of the block size 32.

title: Chapter 4: Troubleshooting IP Addressing — review questions
summary: 4 multiple-choice questions from chapter 4, with answers. 18 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: Step 2 (ping your own IP address) succeeds. What does that prove?
options: The NIC and driver work with the IP stack
questions.why: it proves the IP stack can talk to the NIC. It does not prove the cable is connected.

questions.q: Which command is the Windows version of traceroute?
questions.why: tracert is Windows. traceroute is Cisco, Mac and Linux.

questions.q: A host cannot connect to a remote server. Which test shows whether the NIC is plugged into the network?
questions.why: only the gateway ping proves the local network link works.

questions.q: Which address range is valid for hosts on 192.168.1.64/27?
questions.why: block 32: network 64, broadcast 95, hosts 65-94.

title: Chapter 5: IP Routing — review questions
summary: 4 multiple-choice questions from chapter 5, with answers. 30 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: A router has 10.0.0.0/8 via RIP and 10.1.1.0/24 via a static route. Which route does a packet for 10.1.1.9 use?
options: 10.1.1.0/24, because it is the longest match
Neither, it uses the default route
questions.why: longest prefix match wins first, before administrative distance is even considered.

questions.q: Host A sends to a server on another network. The source and destination MAC addresses of the frame leaving the router towards the server are:
options: Router interface on the server's LAN and the server
Router interface on Host A's LAN and the server
questions.why: the router builds a new frame: its own outgoing interface MAC as source, and the server's MAC as destination.

questions.q: A router learns 172.16.50.0/24 from OSPF and from RIP. Which does it install?
questions.why: lower administrative distance wins when the prefixes are the same.

questions.q: Which command displays the routing table on a Cisco router?
questions.why: show ip route.

title: Chapter 6: Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) — review questions
summary: 7 multiple-choice questions from chapter 6, with answers. 47 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: Which command starts OSPF process 10?
questions.why: router ospf process-id is the command.

questions.q: The OSPF process ID is:
options: The same as the area ID
questions.why: It is only a local label.

questions.q: What is the wildcard mask for 192.168.5.128/27?
questions.why: Block size 32, wildcard 31 (script checked).

questions.q: Hellos are sent to which address?
questions.why: 224.0.0.5 is AllSPFRouters (IANA). 224.0.0.9 is RIPv2 and 224.0.0.10 is EIGRP.

questions.q: On Ethernet, a DROther sends LSA updates to:
questions.why: 224.0.0.6 (AllDRouters). The DR then floods to 224.0.0.5.

questions.q: Default Hello and Dead intervals on an Ethernet link?
questions.why: Hello 10, Dead 40 (4 x Hello). 30/120 is NBMA.

questions.q: Choose three settings that must match for two OSPF routers to become neighbors.
options: Subnet and mask on the link
questions.why: , B, C - Process ID is local, router IDs must differ, priority can differ.

title: Chapter 7: Layer 2 Switching — review questions
summary: 3 multiple-choice questions from chapter 7, with answers. 35 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: Which address does a switch learn from?
questions.why: A Layer 2 switch ignores IP.

questions.q: Which problem is NOT caused by switching loops?
questions.why: Duplicate IPs come from addressing mistakes.

questions.q: Which mode does not shut the port and sends no log or SNMP trap?
questions.why: Restrict logs and traps; shutdown also disables the port.

title: Chapter 8: VLANs and Inter-VLAN Routing — review questions
summary: 12 multiple-choice questions from chapter 8, with answers. 38 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: A switch has 12 active ports and no VLANs configured. How many broadcast domains does it have?
questions.why: with no VLANs the whole switch is one broadcast domain. It has 12 collision domains, one per port.

questions.q: Which statement about 802.1Q is true?
options: It wraps the frame in a new header and a new CRC.
It inserts a 4-byte tag and leaves the native VLAN untagged.
questions.why: 802.1Q is the IEEE standard. A is ISL, B describes ISL, and D confuses 802.1Q with the Cisco normal range.

questions.q: Which of these needs the ip routing command?
questions.why: a multilayer switch only routes once ip routing is turned on. Routers route by default.

questions.q: Which port type sends and receives frames without a VLAN tag?
questions.why: an access port sends untagged frames.

questions.q: How many bytes does an 802.1Q tag add to a frame?
questions.why: 4 bytes. 26 and 30 relate to ISL.

questions.q: Which VLAN carries untagged frames on an 802.1Q trunk by default?
questions.why: the native VLAN, VLAN 1 by default.

questions.q: Which command shows allowed, active and forwarding VLANs on trunks?
questions.why: show vlan brief does not list trunk ports.

questions.q: Two ports are both dynamic auto. Do they trunk?
questions.why: auto waits for the other end to ask.

questions.q: What must be turned on before SVIs route between VLANs on a Layer 3 switch?
questions.why: ip routing.
both are in 192.168.10.16/28 (usable .17 to .30). Calculated by script.

questions.q: True or false: putting hosts in different VLANs makes a network secure by itself.
questions.why: VLAN hopping attacks exist. Set ports to access explicitly, do not use VLAN 1 or native for users, and filter between VLANs.

questions.q: A host in VLAN 10 sends a broadcast. Does a host in VLAN 20 on the same switch receive it?
questions.why: separate VLANs are separate broadcast domains.

title: Chapter 9: Enhanced Switched Technologies — review questions
summary: 12 multiple-choice questions from chapter 9, with answers. 37 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: Which STP states let the switch learn MAC addresses?
questions.why: MAC learning happens in learning and forwarding only.

questions.q: Which STP version is the Cisco IOS default?
questions.why: Book page 261. Rapid PVST+ must be turned on.

questions.q: Which command enables 802.1w on a Cisco switch?
questions.why: Global configuration mode.

questions.q: What happens when a BPDU arrives on a port with PortFast and BPDU Guard?
options: PortFast is disabled and the port keeps working
questions.why: The port is shut down.

questions.q: Which LACP mode combination will not form a channel?
questions.why: Neither side starts negotiation.

questions.q: Does the root bridge have a root port?
questions.why: The root bridge has none; every other switch has exactly one.

questions.q: Which is a valid bridge priority?
questions.why: Multiples of 4096 from 0 to 61440. 20480 = 5 x 4096.

questions.q: What is the default STP hello time?
questions.why: BPDUs go out every 2 seconds.

questions.q: What does protocol ieee mean in show spanning-tree output?
questions.why: In rapid-pvst mode it says rstp.

questions.q: Which feature protects against a new switch winning the root election on a port?
questions.why: Root guard blocks the port when a superior BPDU arrives.

questions.q: Which feature protects against BPDUs suddenly stopping on a non-designated port?
questions.why: Loop guard puts the port in loop-inconsistent instead of letting it forward.

questions.q: Which mode combination will NOT form an LACP channel?
questions.why: Neither side initiates.

title: Chapter 10: Access Lists — review questions
summary: 16 multiple-choice questions from chapter 10, with answers. 46 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: Where would you normally find the web and email servers that the Internet must reach?
questions.why: the DMZ holds the Internet-facing servers.

questions.q: Which of these is an extended ACL number? 55, 150, 1400, 2800
questions.why: 150 is in 100-199. 55 and 1400 are standard. 2800 is outside every range in this chapter.

questions.q: What wildcard mask matches the whole 172.16.0.0/12 private block?
questions.why: a /12 leaves 20 host bits, so the second octet wildcard is 15 and the last two are 255. Script-checked.

questions.q: What is the wildcard mask for a /26?
questions.why: a /26 mask ends in 192, so 255 - 192 = 63. Script-checked.

questions.q: What wildcard matches the Accounting subnet 192.168.10.128/27?
questions.why: a /27 has block size 32, so the wildcard is 31. Script-checked.

questions.q: Which command applies an ACL to the VTY lines?
questions.why: access-class goes under the line, ip access-group goes under an interface.

questions.q: Which protocol keyword must you use to filter FTP?
questions.why: FTP uses TCP. With ip you cannot add a port test.

questions.q: Which command creates a named extended ACL called WEB-ONLY?
questions.why: ip access-list extended <name> opens the named ACL mode.

questions.q: Which command tells you which interface an ACL is applied to?
questions.why: show ip interface shows the in and out lists. show access-list shows the lines only.

questions.q: Which number creates a standard IP ACL?
questions.why: standard is 1-99 and 1300-1999. 100-199 is extended. 2700 is outside the ranges.

questions.q: Which number creates an extended IP ACL?
questions.why: extended is 100-199 and 2000-2699. 99 and 1450 are standard. 2750 is outside the range.

questions.q: A standard ACL can match which part of a packet?
questions.why: standard ACLs check the source IP address only.

questions.q: Which command applies ACL 5 to an interface for packets arriving?
questions.why: ip access-group is the interface command. access-class is for VTY lines.

questions.q: What is the wildcard mask for a /29?
questions.why: 255 - 248 = 7. Script-checked.

questions.q: What is the wildcard mask for a /20?
questions.why: 255 - 240 = 15 in the third octet. Script-checked.

questions.q: Which command shows which interface has an ACL applied and in which direction?
questions.why: show ip interface has the in and out ACL lines. (The running-config also shows it, but is not the best single answer.)

title: Chapter 11: Network Address Translation (NAT) — review questions

questions.q: Which RFC defines the private IPv4 address ranges?
Which address is NOT private?

questions.q: In show cdp neighbors, which column is the neighbor's own interface?

questions.q: Which command makes a router an NTP client of 10.1.1.5?

questions.q: How do you restrict which NMS can use a read-only community?

questions.q: What is severity 4?

questions.q: Which VTY command allows only SSH?

questions.q: Which protocol is Cisco proprietary?

questions.q: Which command lists the neighbor's IP address?

questions.q: Default CDP timer and holdtime?

questions.q: Which command enables LLDP globally?

questions.q: Which UDP port does NTP use?

questions.q: Which SNMP message is sent by the agent without being asked and is not acknowledged?

questions.q: Which SNMP version first offers authentication and encryption?

questions.q: What severity is Notification?

questions.q: What is the default syslog facility on Cisco IOS?

questions.q: Minimum RSA key size for SSH version 2?

questions.q: Which threat type is the hardest to stop, according to the book?

questions.q: Which Cisco IOS feature protects TCP servers from SYN floods?
questions.why: the book's review answer 12.

aaa authentication login local group G

It works only on Cisco devices

title: Chapter 15: Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) — review questions
summary: 22 multiple-choice questions from chapter 15, with answers. 41 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: A host in another city must appear to be on the corporate server VLAN. Which technology fits?
questions.why: a VLAN works for physically local hosts. A VPN extends the local view over a WAN.

questions.q: Which is the current name of Cisco's VPN client that replaced AnyConnect?
questions.why: Cisco's own notice says the current version is now known as Cisco Secure Client.

questions.q: Which two are exam-outline VPN types?
questions.why: and C - remote access and site-to-site are named in the objective. MPLS VPNs are provider services.

questions.q: In a Layer 3 MPLS VPN, which router is yours?
questions.why: CE is the customer edge router. PE and P belong to the provider.

questions.q: At which OSI layer does IPsec work?
questions.why: the book says IPsec works at the Network layer.

questions.q: Which mode is normally used between two sites?
questions.why: gateways protect traffic for the hosts behind them.

questions.q: How many bytes of overhead does GRE add at minimum?
questions.why: 20 bytes of outer IP header plus 4 bytes of GRE header.

questions.q: What is the IP protocol number of GRE?

questions.q: Which technology lets the hub use one tunnel interface and one IPsec profile for all spokes?

questions.q: Which command shows the tunnel source, destination and protocol (GRE/IP)?

questions.q: Which statement best describes a VPN?

A private network created across a public network, using tunnelling and usually encryption

questions.q: A host in a remote office must appear local to a secure server VLAN. Which is the right tool?

questions.q: Which two are enterprise-managed VPN categories?

questions.q: Which IPsec protocol can provide encryption?

questions.q: Which statement about plain IPsec (no GRE) is true according to the book?
options: It carries IP multicast and routing protocols easily
It cannot carry IP broadcast, multicast or non-IP traffic
questions.why: that is why GRE is added to carry routing protocols.

questions.q: Which of these is asymmetric encryption?
questions.why: RSA uses a key pair. The others are symmetric.

questions.q: What is the IP protocol number of GRE?
questions.why: IANA registry. 50 is ESP.

questions.q: Which command creates a GRE tunnel interface numbered 5?

questions.q: Which technology uses one tunnel interface and one IPsec profile on the hub for all spokes, with dynamic spoke-to-spoke tunnels?
questions.why: DMVPN is built from mGRE, NHRP and IPsec. CHECK

title: Chapter 16: Quality of Service (QoS) — review questions
summary: 9 multiple-choice questions from chapter 16, with answers. 21 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: Which QoS problem is the variation in packet delay?
questions.why: jitter is the variation in delay, and it hurts real-time traffic most.

questions.q: Where is the trust boundary in a typical enterprise campus?
questions.why: traffic is classified and marked at the edge before entering the trusted domain.

questions.q: Which is a Layer 2 QoS marking?

questions.q: Which advanced tool classifies applications by looking deep into the payload?

questions.q: Which QoS mechanism drops traffic if a session uses more than its allotted bandwidth?

questions.q: Which queuing mechanism provides both bandwidth and latency guarantees for voice and data?

questions.q: Which of these is a congestion-avoidance mechanism?

questions.q: A user complains that voice calls break up only during large file transfers. Which change best helps?

questions.q: Which statement is true? (Choose one.)
options: Policers delay traffic, shapers drop it
Shapers delay traffic, policers drop or re-mark it

summary: 10 multiple-choice questions from chapter 19, with answers. 49 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: Which 2.4 GHz channels are non-overlapping in the United States?
questions.why: Script check: only 1, 6, 11 fit in channels 1 to 11.

questions.q: Which statement about the 5 GHz band is true compared with 2.4 GHz?
options: Shorter range and more non-overlapping channels
The same range and the same channels
questions.why: Higher frequency travels less far but gives more usable channels.

questions.q: An AP is installed on the ceiling. At minimum, which parameter must be configured so a client can use it?
questions.why: Open authentication needs only the SSID (book question 5).

questions.q: Two laptops connect directly with no AP. What is it called?
questions.why: Independent basic service set (ad hoc).

questions.q: A signal bends around a building and leaves a dead spot. Which behavior is this?
questions.why: Diffraction bends around; refraction bends through different media.

questions.q: Which two encryption methods are based on RC4?
questions.why: , B - AES-CCMP replaced RC4.

questions.q: Which encryption does WPA2 use?
questions.why: SAE is the WPA3-Personal handshake.

questions.q: Which WPA3 feature gives built-in resistance to offline dictionary attacks?
questions.why: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (Dragonfly).

questions.q: Choose two statements that describe WPA.
options: Dynamic encryption keys change during the connection
All devices must use the same static key
questions.why: , C - Book question 17.

questions.q: A client with a b/g card cannot join an 802.11b/g AP, and the AP lists no clients at all. What is a likely reason?
options: Wrong channel set on the client
questions.why: The AP only lists clients that associate. A wrong IP or key would still show an association attempt. A client usually scans all channels itself. CHECK

questions.why: Type 1 is bare-metal.

title: Chapter 22: SDN Controllers — review questions
summary: 15 multiple-choice questions from chapter 22, with answers. 52 further open questions are on the chapter page.

questions.q: Which protocol does an NMS use to poll devices?
questions.why: the book says an NMS polls devices using SNMP.

questions.q: Which command sets the IP address of the syslog server?
questions.why: logging host sets the server. logging trap sets the severity level.

questions.q: Which tool would you use to see what changed in a router's config last night?
questions.why: an NCM can compare saved configuration versions.

questions.q: Which plane does SSH belong to?
questions.why: SSH, Telnet, SNMP and HTTPS are management plane.

questions.q: What is the northbound interface used for?
options: Letting users and scripts interact with the controller
Routing traffic out of the network
questions.why: the NBI is how you reach the controller, usually through a GUI or REST API.

questions.q: Which layer of the campus architecture hosts the SVIs?
questions.why: the distribution layer hosts SVIs, DHCP relay and the Layer 3 boundary.

questions.q: What is the underlay?
options: A layer where tunnels are built to provide services
A layer that provides connectivity throughout the fabric
A term for everything in the SDN network
questions.why: the book's review question 2. Option A is the overlay, and option C is the fabric.

questions.q: What was DNA Center renamed?
questions.why: Cisco's data sheet says Catalyst Center is formerly DNA Center.

questions.q: Which feature configures new switches automatically using Plug and Play?
questions.why: LAN Automation uses PnP with a DHCP server on the upstream device.

questions.q: What do users and scripts use to interact with an SDN controller?
questions.why: the NBI, usually a GUI or REST API.

questions.q: Which statement describes the underlay?
options: The physical Layer 3 network that gives connectivity
A name for all devices in the solution
questions.why: the overlay is the tunnels. The fabric is the term for everything.

questions.q: Which plane runs OSPF and ARP?
questions.why: the control plane runs protocols and builds forwarding information.

questions.q: Which protocol does an NMS mainly use to poll devices?
questions.why: an NMS polls with SNMP.

questions.q: Which command points a router at a syslog server?
questions.why: logging trap sets the severity.

questions.q: Which protocol uses XML over SSH, TCP port 830 by default?
questions.why: RFC 6241 (Cisco IOS XE documentation). It models data with YANG.

The tool makes a change only if the current state differs from the described state

questions.q: Which two configuration management tools require an agent? (Choose two.)

questions.q: What does Ansible call the file that holds the work to be applied to nodes?
questions.why: Playbook. The inventory lists the nodes.

questions.q: Which command runs an Ansible playbook?
questions.why: ansible-playbook. ansible-doc shows module help.
